## UI fidelity supported by this policy

The display policy matches `GradleModuleSystem.kt:646–659` and the default
`AndroidModuleSystem.kt:296`: reported null external project IDs or captured non-Gradle awareness fall back to
the imported internal name; uncaptured external-system identity returns a typed error.
Source-set identities use `GradleProjectResolverUtil.java:531–540`,
root project identities retain the entire external ID, and other project identities
use the final colon component. Exact reported path equality is preserved, including
two null paths; there is no path normalization or case folding.

I checked the important empty-label distinction directly: the source-set helper's
condition is `length < i + 1`, so a trailing colon returns an empty suffix, not null.
The Rust policy and its supplemental cases preserve this behavior. A nonroot
project's trailing delimiter also preserves the empty suffix from `StringUtilRt`.
Null and missing-delimiter fallbacks remain separate from these empty results.
Unicode, whitespace, qualified imported names, and collision suffixes are preserved.

`AndroidViewModuleNode.java:137–156` calls the module display policy for both its
base test string and its visible presentable/bold label. The returned `display_name`
is therefore the appropriate captured display identity for a future node consumer.
The policy does not append `(Android)` to the visible label. The pinned suffix is
in `AndroidModuleNode.kt:74–79`'s test serialization and is explicitly left to a
later node/UI implementation.

The policy keeps holder-group naming separate from the short display label:
`GradleModuleSystem.kt:665` uses `getHolderModule().name`, and the linked-module
helper at `LinkedAndroidModuleGroupUtils.kt:61` can fall back to the module itself.
The policy preserves the supplied authoritative holder name, without guessing or
resolving the holder. `AndroidModuleNode.kt:66–68` uses the imported internal name
for its sort and type-sort key; `sort_name` retains that name even when the external
ID produces a different display label. This task supplies the key, not the complete
IntelliJ comparator or actual UI sorting.

All 20 supplemental test bodies were inspected for these branches and distinct
identities. This review did not execute them and grants no runtime result.
